newsitem.title: GERMANY: German union names wage demand in bank sector.
newsitem.headline: German union names wage demand in bank sector.

text.p: German white-collar workers' trade union DAG on Thursday said it would seek a 1997 wage increase of around 1.7 percent to 1.8 percent for workers in the banking industry.
But DAG chief negotiator Gerhard Renner said the demand could be reduced if employers came forward with measures for improving job security in the industry, which employs around 450,000 workers.

The wage demand follows a decision by German bank employers earlier this month to postpone making controversial cuts to sick payments until a wider wage agreement had been reached, following worker protests in the normally peaceable sector.
Wage increases of 1.5 percent for 1997 have now been agreed for workers in Germany's chemical industry and for the vast majority of workers in the large metal and engineering sectors.
Economists have said that while the wage packages do not offer German companies the labour cost reductions they have been calling for, the settlements can be seen as moderate.
Wage talks in the banking industry are scheduled to start late in January.
